summary: Indiana won 13-6 at Michigan in overtime. Cignetti expects Hoover to be better this week, while the defense and field position remain central before Minnesota visits at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS.

items.headline: Indiana wins 13-6 at Michigan in overtime
items.tldr: Hoover’s four-yard touchdown run supplied the winning score. The next offense needs more sustainable possessions around a defense that kept the game within reach.

items.headline: Cignetti expects Hoover to be better for Minnesota
items.tldr: Monday’s update follows the quarterback’s injury-limited week. It is an expectation, not a guarantee; watch the next availability report and the opening passing rhythm.

items.headline: The defense keeps Michigan out of the end zone
items.tldr: Michigan’s recap shows how its scoring chances ended short of touchdowns. Carry the red-zone assignments forward without asking the defense to erase every stalled offensive drive.

items.headline: Gowers lands three of seven punts inside the 20
items.tldr: The official notes show how the punting unit helped control field position at Michigan. Watch the coverage finish as well as the distance on the next exchange.

items.headline: Minnesota visits Indiana at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS
items.tldr: Saturday’s homecoming game fills the afternoon Eastern window. Confirm the viewing plan before following the quarterback and offensive updates.

lead.headline: Give the defense room to breathe.
lead.body: Create a usable passing answer and sustain the first set of downs. Pair that offensive work with controlled punting coverage and the same red-zone discipline that protects a narrow lead.

matchup.thesis: Make another possession before needing another stop
matchup.question: What should fans watch in the next game?
matchup.answer: Keep protection and receiver separation connected to the quarterback’s release. Take a clean gain early so the next defensive series does not have to carry the whole game.
